title: If a touchscreen is present, trying to select text in a scrolling text container will both select and touch-scroll
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible on tip and on 4.7.2 rc 

Also on 4.7.1 stable, but only when wayland is forced!



### System information

Linux - desktop PC with a USB-C touchscreen as secondary monitor, WAYLAND

### Issue description

On my machine, I can not select text in text containers using the mouse.

When I do so, it both scrolls the container, and selects text, which causes a humorous combination. 

I found the actual culprit for it already. In scroll_bar.cpp, there is a "drag_node_touching" variable being set (~line 595). The thing is, it takes it from `DisplayServer::is_touchscreen_available()` whether or not to use drag mechanics. 

This is a problem when there is a touchscreen available, but touch isn't used! This obviously is also a problem in game builds, selecting in something like a TextBox that has scroll will drag-scroll even with a mouse.

Removing the emulation (touch->mouse or mouse->touch) doesn't change anything, since it still just relies on the above test. 

But, and I'm not sure if this is correct, it seems that the `InputEvent` p_input, marshalled as InputEventMouseButton, always returns a "-1" from get_device() when the input is emulated `InputEvent::DEVICE_ID_EMULATION`. And since ScrollBar only consumes Mouse inputs atm (InputEventMouseButton) and doesn't check for touch input natively, DEVICE_ID_EMULATION would point towards that this input is a touch input. 

This means a simple check if get_device is DEVICE_ID_EMULATION to enable dragging should functionally be fine - at least on PC. I don't know about mobile, though. 

I tried the below attached patch that I made, and for me, this causes it to work mostly as expected: Mouse now is able to select properly, and my extra touchscreen that I have is able to drag scroll (but selects at the same time, which... I think scroll_bar needs to be taught to properly tell apart touch from mouse?)

[scroll-pan-native-touch-only.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30766870/scroll-pan-native-touch-only.patch)

I can draft this into a proper PR if this solution is something you'd consider. It might be flawed in other ways that I can't predict, though...?

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a touchscreen attached to your computer somehow (laptop with touch?)
2. Open editor
3. Cause the "output pane" to have enough entries to be scrollable 
4. Try selecting text with a mouse

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A, reproducible in bare editor

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97f95f97-d76e-4a27-a821-270fbb371224

Additional info: 

```
grep -B1 -A5 "TouchScreen" /proc/bus/input/devices

N: Name="wch.cn TouchScreen"
P: Phys=usb-0000:c5:00.3-1.1/input0
S: Sysfs=/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:08.3/0000:c5:00.3/usb5/5-1/5-1.1/5-1.1:1.0/0003:27C0:0859.0012/input/input39
U: Uniq=9LQ0172005164
H: Handlers=event3 mouse0 
B: PROP=2
```

```
hyprctl monitors | grep -A2 "Monitor "
Monitor DP-1 (ID 0):
	2560x1440@143.97301 at 0x0
	description: LG Electronics LG ULTRAGEAR 105NTHM0H729
--
Monitor DP-4 (ID 2):
	3840x2160@59.99700 at 2560x200
	description: Dell Inc. DELL P2415Q D8VXF69T0EAB
--
Monitor DP-2 (ID 1):
	1920x1200@60.00300 at 300x1440
	description: XYK Display 0x00000004
```

This shows that the touch screen is an additional USB-C screen that also exposes that touchscreen. I can only make it not-recognize by getting rid of it using an UDEV rule (which will "fix" the issue).
